epic.intent:
## Outcome

The chat view becomes a GUI/TUI hybrid. The agent CLI keeps running in its terminal pane, and next to it sit panes the person and the agent share: an embedded browser, a file/image viewer, and an agents pane that shows the agent's subagents live. Images cross between them as files. The person pastes or drops a screenshot into the terminal and the agent gets a path it can read. The agent prints an image path and the person sees it. The agent can open a URL or file in a pane and capture any pane to a PNG, as evidence or to look at its own work.

This is an experiment. Keep each piece small and behind the existing chat view; nothing here changes how runs, tickets or the board work.

## Relation to the image-attachments epic

`ep_01m6fmd1m24pf5nmyke0w4ag6h` (Image attachments) owns storing images as attempt evidence and references (`add_attachment`, the `dm-attachment:` protocol, thumbnails in ticket and card views). This epic does not store evidence. It produces image *files* in a folder that epic already accepts (the system temp folder), so a worker can capture a pane and then `add_attachment` the returned path. Neither epic depends on the other being done first.

## Decisions (my defaults; change before running)

- **Chat image folder:** `<os.tmpdir()>/darkmechanicus/chats/<chatId>/`. Pasted, dropped and captured images go there as `<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>-<n>.png|jpg`. Temp is inside the attachment epic's allowed roots, and the app adds the folder to the Claude settings file it writes (`src/main/terminals/claudeSettingsFile.ts`, `permissions.additionalDirectories`) so Claude Code can read it without a prompt. Files are pruned when a chat is deleted and anything older than 7 days on app start.
- **Image limits:** PNG and JPEG by magic bytes, at most 10 MiB, same as the attachment epic. SVG refused.
- **Browser pane is a `WebContentsView` owned by main, never an iframe or `<webview>`.** The main window keeps `sandbox`, `contextIsolation` and no `webviewTag` (`src/main/index.ts:30-45`); the CSP gains no `frame-src`. The view gets its own session partition per folder, no preload, `sandbox: true`, and its own navigation policy (http, https only; `file:` and custom schemes refused; popups open in the same pane).
- **Agent → app control goes over a local pipe authenticated by the chat's grant.** Today no path exists from a `dm` command to the running app (commands only touch the repo state store). Main listens on a per-instance named pipe (Windows) or Unix socket, puts its address in the PTY environment as `DM_DESKTOP_PIPE`, and accepts a request only with a `DM_SESSION_TOKEN` that main issued for a chat whose PTY is live. The request acts on that chat's panes only.

## Findings from the codebase survey

- Chat terminal: `src/renderer/src/agents/TerminalPane.tsx`, rendered in `MainPane` (`src/renderer/src/App.tsx`, around lines 132 and 191). No split or resizable layout exists anywhere in the renderer.
- xterm 6 with `FitAddon` and `WebglAddon` only (`src/renderer/src/agents/xtermKit.ts`); no link provider. Input goes over a MessagePort (`src/shared/agents/terminalApi.ts`, `src/preload/terminals.ts`); a port message carries at most `TERMINAL_INPUT_MAX_BYTES` = 64 KiB, so image bytes never go over the terminal port.
- Nothing handles paste or drop of images today; clipboard code only writes text (`bootstrap.ts`, `desktop/handlers.ts`).
- No custom protocols, no `WebContentsView`. CSP (`electron.vite.config.ts`, `PROD_CSP`/`DEV_CSP`) allows `img-src 'self' data: file:`; dev serves over http, so `file:` images do not load in dev.
- IPC goes through `guardIpc` (`src/main/ipcGuard.ts`), with narrow methods declared in `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`. The renderer never sends a file path main then reads, except where main checks it against allowed roots.
- `TerminalSessions.paste` (`src/main/terminals/terminalSessions.ts`) already queues bracketed pastes into a PTY; reuse it to type an image path.
- Commands: `src/core/commands/index.ts`, capabilities in `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts` and `src/core/authz.ts`, schemas in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, MCP tools in `src/mcp/tools/*`.
- Design reference: `docs/design/chat-shells.md` (terminal in the window, security of what the renderer can make main do, the chat grant).

## Subagent tracking (sprint 3)

The terminal cutover gave up per-thread worker activity (`docs/design/chat-shells.md`, "Lost, and accepted"). Sprint 3 brings it back without a structured stream: Claude Code writes each subagent to `<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` plus `agent-<id>.meta.json` beside the session transcript (seen on 2.1.318), and the app already knows each chat's session id. Main follows those files read-only and builds an agent tree; the renderer shows it as a pane. Codex follows only if it records enough.

## Risks

- Claude Code's transcript format is not a public contract and changes between versions. Parse defensively, skip what is unknown, and keep fixtures from real files.

- A browser pane in the app can load hostile pages. Keep it in its own partition with no preload and no bridge to the app, and refuse non-web schemes.
- `WebContentsView` draws above the DOM, so app menus and dialogs would sit under it. Hide or detach the view while one is open.
- The control pipe is a new local entry point. Only grants main issued for live chat PTYs may use it, and only on their own chat.
- Captures can contain whatever is on screen. They stay in temp unless an agent attaches one as evidence.

## Standards

Only the project's Definition of Done. No tests-first and no Fireguard in this epic. Each ticket's **Tests** section lists the tests its worker writes and runs.

## Out of scope

- Storing images as evidence or references (the image-attachments epic).
- Drawing or annotating on images.
- Sixel or other inline terminal image protocols.
- More than one side pane at a time, or tabs in the browser pane.

bundle.rationale:
Assumptions:
- Images live in a temp folder per chat, not userData, so Claude Code (via additionalDirectories) and the image-attachments epic's allowed roots both accept them. Pruned after 7 days.
- The browser pane is a WebContentsView in main, so the main window keeps its sandbox and CSP; iframe and <webview> are rejected.
- Agent control uses a local pipe authenticated by the chat's existing grant, since no CLI-to-app path exists. A queue table watched by main was the alternative; the pipe gives synchronous answers (capture returns a path).
- Single side pane, no browser tabs: enough to experiment with.

Graph:
- Sprint 1: split and folder start in parallel; paste follows folder; viewer joins split and folder; links follow viewer; browser follows split.
- Sprint 2: pipe starts at once; commands joins pipe with the sprint-1 panes and folder; capture button joins commands and paste; docs last.
- Sprint 3: the investigation starts at once (it needs nothing from sprints 1-2); the transcript follower follows it; the agents pane joins the follower with the split view and viewer; ticket linking joins follower and pane; Codex (optional) follows the investigation and follower.
- Subagent activity is read from Claude Code's own transcript files rather than hooks or the dm command layer: workers share the orchestrator's grant, so the command layer can't tell them apart, and the files already hold every subagent's tool calls and report. Hooks are added only if the investigation shows the files lag.

tickets.body:
## Context
There is no split or resizable layout in the renderer. `TerminalPane` fills `MainPane` (`src/renderer/src/App.tsx`), sized by CSS and fitted by xterm's `FitAddon` (`src/renderer/src/agents/xtermKit.ts`).

## Do
- Add `src/renderer/src/components/SplitView.tsx`: two children, a draggable divider (pointer events, keyboard arrows on the focused divider, double-click to reset), a minimum width per side (terminal 40 columns' worth, side pane 280 px), and an `onResize` that fires after the drag settles.
- Wrap `TerminalPane` in `MainPane` with it. The side pane is closed by default; a pane toolbar above the terminal has **Browser** and **Viewer** toggles and a close button. Only one side pane at a time.
- Define the pane model in `src/shared/agents/panes.ts`: `PaneKind = 'browser' | 'viewer'`, `PaneState = {kind, url?: string, file?: {token: string, name: string}}`, `ChatLayout = {open: PaneKind | null, ratio: number}`.
- Keep layout per chat in the renderer store and persist it with the chat record (an optional `layout` field on the chat in `src/main/agents/chatStore.ts`; a missing field means closed). No new IPC beyond saving it.
- Refit xterm and send the PTY resize when the divider settles or the window resizes. Keyboard focus stays in the terminal after a drag.
- The side pane renders a placeholder per kind for now; the viewer and browser tickets fill them.

## Tests
`SplitView.test.tsx`: drag and keyboard resize respect both minimums; double-click resets; `onResize` fires once per drag. `App.terminal.test.tsx` (extend): opening and closing a pane refits the terminal and sends one resize; layout is restored when switching back to a chat.

## Context
Pasted, dropped and captured images need one home that Claude Code can read and the image-attachments epic accepts as a source (its allowed roots are the project, the system temp folder and the OS screenshot folder). userData is not one of them, so the folder lives in temp.

## Do
- `src/main/agents/chatImages.ts`:
  - `chatImageDir(chatId)` = `<os.tmpdir()>/darkmechanicus/chats/<chatId>/`, created on demand. Chat ids are validated before use in a path.
  - `inspectImage(bytes)`: PNG or JPEG by magic bytes, width and height from the PNG IHDR or JPEG SOF marker without a new dependency, at most 10 MiB and 8,000 px a side; SVG and anything else refused with a reason. If the image-attachments epic has landed `inspectImageBytes` in `src/core/attachments/intake.ts`, call that instead of duplicating it.
  - `saveChatImage(chatId, bytes, source: 'paste' | 'drop' | 'capture')` writes `<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>-<n>.<ext>` atomically (temp file then rename) and returns the absolute path.
  - `pruneChatImages()`: on app start, delete files older than 7 days; delete a chat's folder when the chat is deleted.
- In `src/main/terminals/claudeSettingsFile.ts`, add the chat's image folder to `permissions.additionalDirectories` in the settings file written at each start, so Claude Code can read images there without asking. Other CLIs get nothing new.

## Tests
`chatImages.test.ts`: accepts PNG and JPEG, refuses SVG, a text file renamed .png, over-size and over-dimension images; names don't collide within one second; prune removes only old files; a bad chat id is refused. `claudeSettingsFile` test (extend): the folder appears in `additionalDirectories`.

tickets.body:
## Context
Nothing handles image paste or drop today. xterm pastes text only, and Electron's Edit menu takes Ctrl+V/Cmd+V first, so an image on the clipboard sends nothing. Image bytes cannot go over the terminal port (64 KiB cap).

## Do
- Add one narrow method to `src/shared/desktop/api.ts`, guarded by `guardIpc`: `chats:attachImage({chatId, source: 'paste' | 'drop' | 'clipboard', bytes?: Uint8Array})`. For `clipboard`, main reads the image itself with `clipboard.readImage()` (PNG); for `paste` and `drop` the renderer sends bytes (at most 10 MiB, refused above). Main calls `saveChatImage`, then `TerminalSessions.paste(chatId, <quoted path> + ' ')` with no Enter, so the person keeps typing their prompt. Returns `{path}` or a problem.
- In `TerminalPane`: handle `paste` (when `clipboardData` has an image item and no text), `dragover`/`drop` of image files (drop of several images pastes each path), and show a brief toast with the file name, or the refusal reason.
- Ctrl+V/Cmd+V with an image-only clipboard: in the terminal's key handler (`keyGoesToTerminal`), when the clipboard holds an image and no text (ask main via a cheap `chats:clipboardHasImage`), call `attachImage` with `clipboard` instead of the normal paste.
- Quote paths for the PTY's shell rules (Windows paths with spaces in double quotes).

## Tests
`App.terminal.test.tsx` or a new `TerminalPane.images.test.tsx`: a paste event with an image item calls `attachImage`; a text paste does not; a drop of two PNGs calls it twice; a refusal shows the reason. Main handler test: bytes over the cap are refused before saving; the PTY receives the quoted path and no carriage return.

tickets.body:
## Context
The renderer cannot load `file:` URLs in dev, and it must not hand arbitrary paths to main. The viewer needs a safe way to show a file the person clicked or the agent opened.

## Do
- Register a privileged scheme `dm-pane:` in main (`protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` before ready, `protocol.handle` after). URLs are `dm-pane://file/<token>`; main keeps a map from opaque token to an absolute path it has already checked. Unknown tokens answer 404. Add `dm-pane:` to `img-src` in both CSPs; do not add `file:` anywhere new.
- Allowed roots for the viewer: the folder's repository root and worktrees, the chat image folder, the system temp folder and the OS screenshot folder (reuse the image-attachments epic's `resolveAllowedRoots` if present, else implement the same rules here). Realpath both sides; refuse links and anything outside.
- Desktop method `panes:openFile({chatId, path})`: main checks the path, issues a token, returns `{token, name, kind: 'image' | 'text' | 'unsupported', bytes}`. Text means UTF-8 under 1 MiB.
- `src/renderer/src/agents/ViewerPane.tsx`: images fit to the pane with zoom (wheel, 100%/fit buttons) and pan; text files in a read-only monospace view; file name, size and an **Open in system** button (existing openExternal path, through main's check). The pane's state is `{kind: 'viewer', file: {token, name}}`.

## Tests
Main: path inside each root accepted, outside refused, symlink refused, unknown token 404, a token for one chat works only while the app runs. Renderer: `ViewerPane.test.tsx` renders an image and a text file and the zoom controls.

reasoning.rationale: New protocol and path checks are a security boundary between the renderer and the file system.

tickets.body:
## Context
The terminal has no link provider. Agents and tools print paths like `C:\Users\...\shot.png` or `docs/design/mockups/x.png`; today the person has to go find them.

## Do
- In `xtermKit.ts`, register an xterm link provider (`terminal.registerLinkProvider`) that matches absolute paths and repository-relative paths ending in `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` (case-insensitive), including Windows drive paths, quoted paths and paths wrapped across lines. Keep the regex in `src/renderer/src/agents/imagePathLinks.ts` so it is unit tested.
- Hover: ask main `panes:openFile` (from the viewer ticket) and show a small thumbnail tooltip (max 240 px) through `dm-pane:`; a refused path shows the reason in the tooltip.
- Click (or Ctrl+click, matching xterm's link conventions): open the viewer pane with that file.
- Relative paths resolve against the chat's folder in main, never in the renderer.

## Tests
`imagePathLinks.test.ts`: Windows, POSIX, quoted, spaced and relative paths matched; `.svg`, URLs and partial words not matched. A renderer test that hovering a link requests the file and clicking opens the viewer pane.

tickets.body:
## Context
The main window is sandboxed with `contextIsolation` and no `webviewTag` (`src/main/index.ts:30-45`), and `hardenWebContents` restricts its navigation. An iframe would need `frame-src` in the CSP and would share the app's renderer; use a `WebContentsView` instead.

## Do
- `src/main/panes/browserPane.ts`: one `WebContentsView` per chat with a browser pane open, attached to the main window's `contentView`. `webPreferences`: no preload, `sandbox: true`, `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `partition: 'persist:dm-browser-<folder key>'`.
- Navigation policy on the view: allow `http:` and `https:` only (localhost included, for dev servers); refuse `file:`, `dm-pane:`, `devtools:` and anything else; `setWindowOpenHandler` opens popups in the same view; downloads are cancelled with a notice; permission requests (camera, notifications, etc.) denied.
- Desktop methods: `panes:browser:navigate({chatId, url})`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `setBounds({chatId, rect})` (the renderer reports the side pane's rectangle on layout changes; main clamps it to the window), `hide`/`show`. Main pushes `{url, title, canGoBack, canGoForward, loading}` updates to the renderer.
- `src/renderer/src/agents/BrowserPane.tsx`: address bar (a bare host or `localhost:5173` gets a scheme), back, forward, reload, a loading bar, and the reported title. A ResizeObserver keeps the bounds in sync.
- The view draws above the DOM: hide it while an app menu, dialog or the sign-in overlay is open, and when the chat is not shown; show it again after.
- Destroy the view when its pane closes, its chat is deleted or the window closes.

## Tests
Main: the navigation policy allows http/https and refuses the other schemes; popups stay in the view; bounds are clamped. Renderer: `BrowserPane.test.tsx` sends navigate with a normalised URL and reports bounds on resize.

reasoning.rationale: Embedding untrusted web content in the app; isolation and navigation policy must be right.

tickets.body:
## Context
No path exists today from a `dm` command to the running desktop app; commands only act on the repo state store. Each chat PTY already gets a `DM_SESSION_TOKEN` grant main issued when it started and revokes when it exits (`docs/design/chat-shells.md` §3, `src/main/agents/chatGrants.ts`).

## Do
- `src/main/panes/controlPipe.ts`: on app start, listen on a per-instance named pipe (`\\.\pipe\darkmechanicus-<random>` on Windows) or a Unix socket in a user-only folder (mode 0700). Put its address in each chat PTY's environment as `DM_DESKTOP_PIPE`.
- Protocol: one JSON request per line, `{token, op, args}`, one JSON answer per line, `{ok, data}` or `{ok: false, error: {code, message}}`. Requests over 64 KiB are refused.
- Authentication: hash the token and look it up among grants main issued for chats whose PTY is running. The grant's chat is the only chat the request may act on. Anything else answers `unauthorized`; nothing is logged with the token.
- Ops for now: `panes.open`, `panes.capture`, `panes.state` with handlers that the next ticket implements; this ticket wires a `ping` op and the dispatcher.
- Client: `src/core/desktop/desktopClient.ts` (pure Node, `net.connect`) that reads `DM_DESKTOP_PIPE` and `DM_SESSION_TOKEN` from the environment, with a 10 s timeout. No pipe in the environment means `desktop_unavailable`.

## Tests
`controlPipe.test.ts`: a live chat's token gets `ping` back; a revoked token, a token for an exited PTY, a malformed line and an oversized request are refused; two chats can't act on each other. `desktopClient.test.ts`: timeout and `desktop_unavailable`.

reasoning.rationale: A new local entry point into the app; authentication and scoping must hold.

tickets.body:
## Context
Commands live in `src/core/commands/index.ts` with capabilities in `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts` / `src/core/authz.ts`, schemas in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`, and MCP tools in `src/mcp/tools/*` (shown only when the role holds the capability).

## Do
- New capability `pane.control`, held by the orchestrator and worker roles.
- `open_in_pane({url} | {path}, pane?: 'browser' | 'viewer')`: a URL opens the browser pane (http/https only, by the browser pane's policy); a path opens the viewer (checked against the viewer's allowed roots in main). Opens the side pane if closed. Returns the pane state.
- `capture_pane({pane: 'browser' | 'viewer' | 'terminal' | 'window', waitForLoad?: boolean})`: main captures with `webContents.capturePage()` (the browser view for `browser`; the main window cropped to the pane's rectangle for `viewer` and `terminal`; the whole window for `window`), saves it with `saveChatImage(..., 'capture')`, and returns `{path, width, height, url?, title?, capturedAt}`. `waitForLoad` waits up to 15 s for the browser to finish loading.
- `get_pane_state()`: open pane, URL, title, file name, sizes.
- All three go through `desktopClient` and answer `desktop_unavailable` outside an app chat terminal. They never write to the repo state store.
- Implement the `panes.*` ops behind the control pipe in main.

## Tests
Command tests with a fake desktop client: schema validation, `desktop_unavailable`, capability checks. Main op tests: open refuses `file:` URLs and out-of-root paths; capture writes a valid PNG to the chat image folder and returns its path; capturing a closed pane is refused with a reason.

## Context
The person should be able to hand the agent what they see without saving files by hand.

## Do
- Add a **Capture** button to the pane toolbar (captures the open side pane) and to the terminal's toolbar menu (**Capture terminal**, **Capture window**). It uses the same main capture as `capture_pane` and pastes the quoted path into the PTY via `TerminalSessions.paste` without Enter, like an image paste.

tickets.body:
## Do
- `docs/design/hybrid-workspace.md`: the pane model, the chat image folder and its pruning, the `dm-pane:` protocol, the browser pane's isolation and navigation policy, the control pipe and its authentication, and how captures feed the image-attachments epic's `add_attachment`.
- `docs/runbooks/cli.md`: `open_in_pane`, `capture_pane`, `get_pane_state`, `desktop_unavailable`.
- Role guides (`skills/orchestrator.md`, `skills/worker.md`, the reviewer guide): a worker checking UI work opens the page or file, captures it, reads the capture, and attaches it as evidence when attachments exist. The instructions file written for each chat mentions the panes in one short paragraph.

tickets.body:
## Context
The terminal cutover removed per-thread worker activity on purpose (`docs/design/chat-shells.md`, "Lost, and accepted": "per-thread activity for worker subagents"). The person now wants it back. The app no longer gets a structured stream, so subagent activity must come from what the CLI writes to disk or reports through hooks.

What is already known for Claude Code (seen on 2.1.318, Windows):
- The session transcript is `~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/<session id>.jsonl`; the app already knows the session id (it starts Claude with `--session-id`).
- Each subagent has `<session id>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl` (records with `isSidechain: true`, `agentId`, `sessionId`, `type` user/assistant/attachment/api-request...) and `agent-<agentId>.meta.json` (`agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth`, `requestShape` foreground/background, `effort`, `pickedEffortModel`, `finished`).
- In the parent transcript, the tool result of the spawn carries `toolUseResult` with `agentId`, `status`, `description`, `resolvedModel`, `prompt`, `isAsync`.
- The app already writes a Claude settings file with a `PreToolUse` hook (`src/main/terminals/claudeSettingsFile.ts`), so adding hooks is possible.

## Do
- Confirm the layout above: nested subagents (`spawnDepth` > 1), a subagent that fails or is stopped, a resumed session, and a chat on `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Note what changes the transcript format between versions (`version` on each record) and how far the files lag the screen.
- Check whether `SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` hooks exist on the installed version and what their input carries, and whether they add anything the files don't (lower latency, a stop reason).
- Codex and Autonomous: find what they record for subagents, if anything (Codex rollout files under `~/.codex/sessions`), and say plainly where nothing is available.
- Write the model in `docs/design/agent-activity.md` and as types in `src/shared/agents/agentActivity.ts`: `AgentNode {id, parentId, depth, kind ('root' | 'subagent'), type, description, model, effort, background, status ('running' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'stopped' | 'unknown'), startedAt, endedAt?, tokens?, toolCalls: number, current?: string, report?: string, ticketKey?}` and `AgentEvent` (tool call started/finished with tool name, short input summary, ok/error, timestamps). The parser ticket implements it.

## Tests
None; this is an investigation. Commit the doc and the types (types compile).

tickets.body:
## Context
Uses the model and findings from the investigation ticket. Main knows each Claude chat's session id and folder.

## Do
- `src/main/agents/activity/claudeTranscripts.ts`: locate the session transcript and its `subagents/` folder from the chat's session id, the folder's canonical path (Claude's directory encoding) and the Claude config folder (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`). Watch the folder (`fs.watch` with a 1 s poll fallback, since Windows watches can drop events) and read each JSONL file incrementally from its last offset; a partial last line waits for the rest.
- `src/main/agents/activity/agentTree.ts`: fold records into `AgentNode`s and `AgentEvent`s: a subagent appears when its `meta.json` or first record appears; tool calls pair `tool_use` with `tool_result`; `finished` in `meta.json`, or the parent's spawn result, ends it; its final assistant text is `report`; tokens add up from usage. Unknown record types and versions are skipped, never fatal.
- Mask claim tokens in everything kept (`src/main/agents/claimTokenMask.ts`). Tool inputs are summarised (tool name plus the first 120 characters of the main argument), never kept whole.
- Keep at most 2,000 events per chat in memory; older events are dropped from memory but the counts stay right.
- Start following when a Claude chat's PTY starts, stop when the chat is deleted or the app quits. A chat started before the app (on resume) is read from the start of its files.
- Desktop methods: `agents:tree({chatId})` returns the nodes; `agents:events({chatId, agentId, before?})` pages events; main pushes `agents:changed` (debounced 250 ms) to attached frames.
- If the investigation found hooks needed, add them to the settings file here, writing to the same tree.

## Tests
Fixture transcripts (trimmed real files, tokens replaced) in `src/main/agents/activity/__fixtures__/`: a foreground and a background subagent, a nested subagent, a failed one, a partial last line, an unknown record type. `agentTree.test.ts` checks the tree, statuses, tool pairing, reports and token totals; `claudeTranscripts.test.ts` checks incremental reads and the path encoding on Windows and POSIX; a masking test checks a claim token in a tool input never appears.

## Context
Worker subagents run on the orchestrator's grant, so the command layer cannot tell them apart (`chat-shells.md`, panels that follow a chat). The transcript can: the orchestrator's spawn prompt names the ticket, and the run's claim gives the attempt.

## Do
- In `agentTree.ts`, set `ticketKey` on a subagent when its spawn prompt or description names a ticket or card key of this folder (`DM-123`) or an attempt id the orchestrator claimed in the same session (from its `claim_ticket` / `claim_kanban_card` calls in the parent transcript). When several keys appear, prefer the attempt id, then the first key in the description. Record how it was matched.
- Ticket and Kanban card Activity tabs: list the subagents bound to that ticket (status, description, elapsed, report preview) with **Show in chat**, which opens the chat with the agents pane and that subagent selected.
- The orchestrator kickoff and `skills/orchestrator.md`: when spawning a worker, put the ticket key at the start of the subagent's description (e.g. `DM-452 paste images`), so the match is exact.

## Tests
`agentTree.test.ts` (extend): binding by attempt id, by key in the description, by key in the prompt, and no binding for a key from another folder. A renderer test for the Activity tab list and Show in chat.
